canonical_statement: Let (M,g) be a smooth closed Riemannian manifold of dimension n at least 3. There exists a smooth positive function u on M such that the conformal metric u^(4/(n-2)) g has constant scalar curvature.
domain_and_universes: A smooth compact manifold M without boundary, a Riemannian metric g, and natural dimension n = dim(M) with 3 <= n; exact Lean universes and typeclasses remain open.
quantifiers: for every smooth closed Riemannian manifold (M,g)
there exists a smooth function u : M -> Real
hypotheses: M is compact and has no boundary
g is a smooth Riemannian metric
conclusion: The scalar curvature of the conformally rescaled metric u^(4/(n-2)) g is constant on M.

alternate_encodings.target: A positive smooth solution of the Yamabe equation L_g u = lambda * u^((n+2)/(n-2))
alternate_encodings.relationship: classically equivalent through the scalar-curvature conformal-change formula
alternate_encodings.checked_witness: none; candidate transport deferred to statement phase

alternate_encodings.target: The conformal class of g contains a metric attaining its Yamabe invariant
alternate_encodings.relationship: variational formulation, subject to normalization and regularity hypotheses
alternate_encodings.checked_witness: none; candidate transport deferred to statement phase

excluded_degenerate_cases: Dimensions 0, 1, and 2 are outside this theorem; manifolds with boundary and noncompact manifolds require different statements. Disconnected closed manifolds need an explicit convention for one global constant and are not silently resolved at intake.
